conditions.browser: Chromium (Playwright build), macOS system fonts, deviceScaleFactor 1

candidates.name: d1r4A
candidates.idea: 将所属行业加宽至56px，尝试让行业名称和表头按两个汉字换行，同时保留名称列的两字宽度。所需6px从成交额列取得；需在渲染中检查较窄表头是否仍能保持“（亿）”完整，以及成交额数值是否完整。
candidates.label: gold

whys: Codes, prices and percentages stay whole, and two-character industry entries fit on one line. Consistent row heights support comparison, though company names wrap and the turnover header breaks awkwardly over four lines.

Stock codes and numerical values stay whole, while names and industries generally wrap in readable pairs. Uniform data-row heights aid scanning. The four-line 成交额（亿） header, with its isolated closing parenthesis, remains awkward.

Codes and financial values remain whole, industries mostly read in pairs of characters, and uniform body rows support comparison. Company names still wrap, and the turnover header breaks across four lines with an isolated closing parenthesis.

candidates.name: d2r4A
candidates.idea: 保留d2r2A中较易识别的两字一行股票名称，将行业列收窄9px并转给成交额列。成交额数值和“（亿）”应能完整显示，代价是行业名称更可能逐字换行；需通过渲染核实。
candidates.label: acceptable

whys: Codes and numeric values remain intact, and names generally occupy two lines. The narrow industry column stacks characters vertically and makes the last rows disproportionately tall.

Codes and numeric values are intact, and company names mostly wrap in pairs of characters. The industry column is too narrow: its header and entries such as 半导体 and 汽车整车 stack one character per line, extending the last rows.
Codes and financial values remain whole, and names are more readable than in A. The industry column still runs one character per line, producing very tall final rows and making industry lookup slow.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Equal widths fit the viewport but leave too little text space for the longest stock code, price and percentage change. Those identifiers and figures would have to break or overflow, impairing lookup and comparison.
candidates.label: bad

whys: Stock codes, prices and percentages break across lines, making lookup and comparison difficult. Equal columns leave some numeric cells spacious while splitting essential identifiers.

The equal columns split stock codes, prices and percentage signs across lines, making lookup and comparison laborious. The rows are consistent in height, but that regularity comes at a substantial reading cost.
The compact rows come at the cost of splitting every stock code and several prices and percentages. Those breaks seriously impair lookup and comparison; the turnover header also breaks awkwardly.
Codes and numeric values stay whole, but company names and industries run almost character by character down very tall rows. The resulting empty space makes scanning across rows slow.

Codes and numeric values remain whole, but company names and industries run one character per line. The resulting tall rows make it difficult to scan related fields and leave large empty areas in the numeric columns.
Codes and figures stay intact, but company names and industries run one character per line. The resulting tall rows make scanning and comparing stocks laborious.

d1.purpose: 展示部分A股个股的行情与行业归属，供读者快速查询和横向比较。
tasks: 按股票代码或名称定位个股，横向读取其价格、涨跌幅、成交额、市盈率和所属行业。
纵向比较个股的价格、涨跌幅、成交额及市盈率。
逐行浏览股票，了解行情与行业的对应关系。
relations: 代码和名称共同标识个股；同一行的行情指标与行业均属于该股票。
最新价、涨跌幅、成交额和市盈率是不同的比较指标；成交额表头中的“亿”是单位。
roles: 首行是列标题，应清楚标明指标和单位；后六行各代表一只股票。
代码列是行标题和主要定位依据，名称列提供另一种识别方式。
四个行情指标列支持纵向比较，所属行业列提供分类信息。
keep_whole: 价格、涨跌幅及其他数值中的连续数字和符号。
表头中的“亿”及其括号应作为单位整体阅读。
may_wrap: 股票名称和行业名称可按汉字自然换行，但应尽量减少拆分。
较长的成交额表头可以换行，单位宜保持完整。
市盈率中可在内容允许的断点处换行，仍需保持数值易于辨认。
same_scale: 代码、最新价和涨跌幅列都需要容纳完整的识别码或数值，应保持足够且相近的可用宽度。
名称和所属行业均为中文分类文字，可根据其查找作用和换行代价分配不同宽度。
d1.h_vs_v: 完整单行显示所有内容超过视口；优先保证代码及关键行情数值完整，以中文名称、行业和长表头的适度换行换取无横向滚动的阅读，同时控制行高增长。

d2.purpose: 在有限宽度内呈现部分A股个股的行情和行业归属，供读者按股票查阅和横向比较。
tasks: 按代码或名称定位股票
比较最新价、涨跌幅、成交额和市盈率
relations: 每行的代码和名称共同标识一只股票，其余单元格描述同一只股票
最新价、涨跌幅、成交额和市盈率是需要跨行比较的数值
成交额标题中的“亿”是数值单位，应与指标名称保持明确关联
roles: 首列代码为行标题，是稳定的查找锚点
四个行情指标列用于读取和比较数值
表头标识各列含义，成交额表头同时给出单位
keep_whole: 价格、百分比及其他数值的完整表示，包括符号、小数点和千位分隔符
成交额单位“亿”与其括号
may_wrap: 股票名称和行业名称可在汉字之间换行，但应尽量保持连续易读
较长表头可换行，成交额名称与单位应保持相邻
same_scale: 代码、最新价和涨跌幅列需按各自不可拆分内容的宽度保证可读性
名称与行业同为中文分类或标识文本，可根据查找任务分配相近或有侧重的宽度
数值列的宽度应反映各自内容，而非强求相等
d2.h_vs_v: 总宽度不足以让所有内容单行显示；优先保证代码和数值完整，以中文名称、行业和较长表头的换行换取无横向滚动的阅读体验。

d3.purpose: 展示部分A股个股的行情和所属行业，供读者按股票查阅并横向比较。
tasks: 通过代码或名称定位股票
比较最新价、涨跌幅、成交额和市盈率
relations: 每行的代码和名称共同标识一只股票，其余单元格描述该股票的行情或行业
成交额表头中的“亿”是该列数值的单位
涨跌幅的正负号和百分号是数值含义的一部分
roles: 首行为列标题，说明各字段及单位
代码列为行标题，是稳定的查找入口
名称和所属行业是中文标签；中间四列是可比较的数值字段
keep_whole: 六位股票代码，包括开头的零
价格、带符号的百分比、成交额和市盈率数值
小数点、正负号和百分号与各自数值
may_wrap: 股票名称和行业名称可按汉字换行，但应尽量保持名称易于连续辨认
列标题可在适当位置换行；成交额与其单位应保持明确关联
same_scale: 四个行情数值列应有相近的视觉分量，并按各自内容宽度调整
名称与行业都是中文标签，可根据定位股票和识别行业的相对重要性分配空间
d3.h_vs_v: 496px内无法让所有内容保持单行；优先保证代码和数值完整，用中文标签及表头换行换取水平空间。标签列越窄，行高和纵向查找距离越大。

analysis.strengths: 代码、价格和涨跌幅保持完整，便于逐行查找和比较；行业名称至多两行，数据行高度一致，表格完整放入视口。
analysis.faults: 成交额表头被拆成四行，右括号单独占一行；股票名称均需换行，部分名称和行业词语被拆开。表头因此显得过高。
analysis.spatial_logic: 优先保证代码和数值列的不可拆分内容完整，再把余宽分给名称、成交额、市盈率和行业。行业列保留了容纳两个汉字的空间，使数据行保持紧凑。

analysis.strengths: 代码和主要数值仍保持完整；成交额表头分成两行，名称与单位的关系更清楚。
analysis.faults: 行业列过窄，所属行业表头逐字分行，白酒、电池等词也被拆开；较长行业名称使末两行明显增高，查阅和比较受到干扰。
analysis.spatial_logic: 从行业列移出6px给成交额列，换取更好的成交额表头，却使行业列只能容纳单个汉字，导致多处断词和行高增加。

rounds.insights: 这张表的宽度非常紧张：代码和数值需要保留完整，中文列至少容纳两个汉字则能显著改善连续阅读。Q说明改善单个表头可能以整列内容和整体高度为代价；P的成交额表头虽然不理想，但它更好地服务于逐行查找和比较。

bad.why: The industry column is too narrow: it breaks industry names into single characters, making lookup harder and increasing the last two row heights. Its wider turnover column improves the header, but at too great a cost to the body.

contrast.why: Equal widths fit the viewport but leave too little text space for the longest stock code, price and percentage change. Those identifiers and figures would have to break or overflow, impairing lookup and comparison.

sameFunctionGroups.why: Both identify the stock, but codes must remain whole while Chinese names can wrap; they need different widths.
These are quantitative measures, but their values and headers have different width needs. Each should receive enough space for its own figures.

synthesis.rationale: P keeps stock codes and numeric values intact and gives industry names room to read in short groups. Q improves the turnover header but reduces the industry column to one character per line, adding substantial height and making comparison harder. P still has an awkward four-line turnover header and wrapped names, so it is a constrained choice.

general: Protect identifiers and numeric values from disruptive breaks.
Allocate width according to content and lookup tasks, not equal column widths.
Judge header improvements against their effect on all body rows.
specific: At 496px, the code, latest price and change columns need most of their allocated widths to keep their longest values whole.
The six pixels moved from industry to turnover in Q cause repeated character-by-character wrapping and two taller body rows.

synthesis.tradeoffs: P sacrifices a natural turnover header and keeps several stock and industry names on multiple lines. Q gains a clearer turnover header but substantially worsens the industry column.
synthesis.uncertain: Only P and Q were rendered for comparison; another width allocation within the viewport might produce a better balance.

critique.good: 代码、价格和涨跌幅完整且便于纵向比较；股票名称按两字一行排列，成交额单位保持完整。三案中整体高度最低。
critique.problems: 所属行业逐字竖排，表头占四行；较长行业也占三至四行，使表头和末尾行过高，行业难以快速辨认。市盈率表头也被拆开。
critique.cause: 所属行业列仅41px，文本可用宽度约20px；市盈率列60px，不足以容纳三字表头。

critique.good: 代码和关键数值完整；行业多以两字为一行，比A更容易阅读，表头高度也较低。
critique.problems: 股票名称逐字竖排，破坏主要查找入口的连续阅读，并使各行很高；名称表头也被拆开。
critique.cause: 名称列仅45px，文本可用宽度约24px；行业列增至61px是以名称列宽度为代价的。

critique.good: 代码及关键行情数值完整，成交额单位保持完整。
critique.problems: 名称和行业大多逐字竖排，行业表头占四行；高行与大量空白削弱横向浏览和比较。成交额列的额外宽度未改善其两行表头。
critique.cause: 名称列43px、行业列48px均不足以并排容纳两个汉字；成交额列88px仍不足以单行容纳完整表头，却占用了可供文字列使用的宽度。

critique.good: 代码、最新价和涨跌幅完整，行业名称大多能按两个汉字一行阅读；表格适合视口。
critique.problems: 多数股票名称被逐字拆成三四行，使表格过高、行间比较费力。成交额表头中的单位被拆开，且68.42断行，妨碍读取数值。
critique.cause: 名称列55px不足以容纳两个汉字；成交额列65px不足以完整显示所有数值和单位。

critique.good: 股票名称多以两个汉字一行显示，成交额数值和单位完整；表格较紧凑，行情指标便于纵向比较。
critique.problems: 行业列的标题和内容逐字竖排，汽车整车占四行，削弱了行业查找和逐行阅读；市盈率标题也断行。
critique.cause: 行业列仅41px，无法容纳两个汉字；市盈率列60px不足以完整显示三字标题。

critique.good: 代码、价格、涨跌幅、成交额和市盈率均保持完整，便于定位股票和纵向比较；成交额表头的单位也保持完整。
critique.problems: 行业表头逐字竖排，行业名称多处拆成单字，使后两行明显增高；股票名称也普遍分成两行。
critique.cause: 行业列仅 50px，容不下两个汉字；名称列 56px 只能容纳约两个汉字。

critique.good: 行业列能以两个汉字为一行，表身各行高度一致，行业信息更容易浏览。
critique.problems: 成交额 68.42 被拆成两行，妨碍数值辨认和比较；成交额表头也被拆成四行，单位括号分离。
critique.cause: 成交额列缩至 65px，既不足以容纳最长数值，也不足以让表头和单位在合适的位置换行。

critique.good: 代码和各项行情数值完整，成交额表头及单位清楚。
critique.problems: 名称列加宽后仍需换行，却使行业列更窄；行业表头和名称逐字竖排，后两行过高。
critique.cause: 名称列为 65px，仍不足以单行容纳最长名称；行业列仅 41px，空间明显不足。

critique.good: 表格适合视口；代码、价格和涨跌幅保持完整，便于定位和纵向比较。成交额表头的单位也保持在一起。
critique.problems: 股票名称和行业名称大多逐字换行，行业表头排成四行。高行距使同行数据之间产生大片空白，连续阅读和横向查找都较费力。
critique.cause: 名称列51px、所属行业列55px，均不足以稳定容纳两个汉字；市盈率列60px也使其表头换行。

critique.good: 名称列加宽后，股票名称多以两个汉字为一行，表格明显缩短；代码和关键数值完整，适合视口。
critique.problems: 所属行业仍逐字换行，最后两行尤其高；四行的行业表头也拉高了整个表头。市盈率表头分成两行。
critique.cause: 所属行业列仅50px，无法容纳两个汉字；市盈率列60px不足以单行容纳表头。

critique.good: 表格恰好适合视口；股票代码、价格和涨跌幅完整显示，数值便于纵向比较。名称和行业大多以两字为单位换行，六个数据行高度一致，逐行查阅较顺畅。
critique.problems: 成交额表头被拆成四行，右括号单独占一行，单位难以整体辨认，也使表头过高。名称和部分行业需要换行。
critique.cause: 成交额列宽67px不足以完整容纳“（亿）”；名称和行业列各56px，只能容纳约两个汉字。

critique.good: 成交额列加宽后，表头中的“（亿）”保持完整；代码和主要行情数值仍保持单行，表格也适合视口。
critique.problems: 所属行业表头逐字竖排，行业名称也被逐字拆开；较长行业使末两行明显增高，破坏行间节奏和横向查阅效率。
critique.cause: 为成交额列增加6px，将所属行业列缩至50px，可用文本宽度不足以容纳两个汉字。

critique.good: 代码和各项数值保持完整，成交额的名称与单位相邻，表格适合在视口内查看。
critique.problems: 名称和行业逐字竖排，查找股票和读取分类都很费力；四行高的表头和大量高行使数值比较缺乏紧凑性。市盈率标题也被拆开。
critique.cause: 名称列和行业列均为50px，文字区不足以容纳两个汉字；市盈率列66px仍不足以让标题单行显示。

critique.good: 名称多以两字一组换行，股票识别比A和C顺畅；代码及数值完整，多数数据行高度一致，横向比较较容易。成交额名称和单位分两行但关联清楚。
critique.problems: 行业逐字竖排，尤其“汽车整车”占四行，拉高末行；行业表头同样占四行，造成表头与数据区的大块空白。市盈率标题断成两行。
critique.cause: 行业列仅41px，文字区只能容纳一个汉字；名称列65px则容纳两个汉字。市盈率列60px不足以容纳完整标题。

critique.good: 行业以两字为单位读取，常见的两字行业保持完整；表头较低，代码和数值完整。
critique.problems: 股票名称逐字竖排，削弱按名称定位的主要任务，并拉高多数数据行；名称表头和市盈率表头也换行。
critique.cause: 名称列仅41px，只能容纳一个汉字；行业列65px获得了两字宽度，但这一分配使更频繁用于定位的名称列过窄。

critique.good: 代码、价格、涨跌幅和其他数值均保持完整，数值列便于纵向比较，表格也恰好适合视口。
critique.problems: 名称和行业大多逐字竖排，股票识别和行业查阅都很费力；四行高的行业表头使表头过高，数据行也显得疏松。
critique.cause: 名称列 55px 和行业列 51px 均不足以容纳两个汉字；市盈率列 60px 也使三字表头换行。

critique.good: 名称多以两个汉字一组换行，股票更容易识别；代码和数值完整，整体高度明显低于 d2r1A。
critique.problems: 行业仍逐字竖排，尤其“汽车整车”占四行；所属行业表头同样占四行，造成较高表头和局部过高的数据行。名称中的部分词组仍被拆开。
critique.cause: 行业列只有 41px，仅能容纳单个汉字；名称列 65px 可容纳两个汉字，但不足以完整容纳最长名称。

critique.good: 代码、最新价和涨跌幅完整，名称与行业大多以两个汉字一组换行；各数据行等高，便于横向查阅。表格恰好适合视口。
critique.problems: 成交额中的68.42和74.86被拆行，妨碍比较；表头“成交额（亿）”被拆成四行，括号也被分开，造成过高的表头和不自然的阅读节奏。
critique.cause: 成交额列64px不足以容纳最长数值或完整的“（亿）”；名称列56px和行业列59px则勉强容纳两个汉字。

critique.good: 成交额数值完整，表头分为“成交额”和“（亿）”，指标与单位的关系清楚；代码、价格及涨跌幅也完整。
critique.problems: 行业名称逐字竖排，行业表头四行，末两行明显增高，查找和跨行比较都受到干扰。名称仍需换行，增加的宽度没有带来明显收益。
critique.cause: 行业列仅41px，只能容纳一个汉字；名称列65px仍不足以容纳大多数完整名称，却占用了可供行业列使用的空间。

critique.good: 表格适应视口；代码、行情数值和成交额单位均完整显示。成交额标题分成指标和单位两行，关系清楚。
critique.problems: 股票名称和行业几乎逐字竖排，多个表头也被拆开；行高很大，横向比较需要跨越大片空白。
critique.cause: 名称列仅51px、行业列仅55px，均不足以容纳两个汉字并排；市盈率列60px也使表头换行。

critique.good: 名称和行业大多以两字为一行，行与行之间更紧凑，股票定位和跨行比较明显更容易。代码、最新价和涨跌幅完整。
critique.problems: 成交额数值被拆行，影响数值读取和比较；成交额标题被拆成四行，括号与单位分离，并抬高了整行表头。市盈率表头也换行。
critique.cause: 成交额列64px不足以容纳最长数值和完整的“（亿）”；市盈率列60px不足以单行容纳表头。

critique.good: 代码和行情数值完整，成交额标题的名称与单位分行但保持相邻；股票名称大多按两个汉字一组换行。
critique.problems: 行业列逐字竖排，尤其是“半导体”和“汽车整车”，使阅读和跨行查找费力，也拉高了表头及后两行。
critique.cause: 行业列为50px，扣除内边距和边框后不足以容纳两个汉字。

critique.good: 行业列多数内容可按两个汉字一组阅读，六个数据行高度一致，整体更紧凑。
critique.problems: 成交额中的68.42和74.86被拆开，妨碍数值比较；成交额标题的括号和单位也被拆散。
critique.cause: 成交额列缩至64px，无法容纳最长数值，也不足以保持“（亿）”完整。

critique.good: 代码和行情数值完整，便于按行查找和比较；成交额与单位的关系清楚，表格也恰好适合视口。
critique.problems: 名称和行业几乎逐字竖排，股票名称难以连续辨认，造成大面积空白和很长的查找距离。所属行业表头也占了四行。
critique.cause: 名称列 55px、行业列 51px 都不足以在当前字体和内边距下容纳两个汉字。

critique.good: 名称大多按两个汉字换行，比 A 更容易辨认，表格也明显更紧凑。
critique.problems: 000858、1,438.00、+3.56% 和 112.3 被拆开，损害股票定位和数值比较。行业逐字竖排，成交额表头的右括号单独占行。
critique.cause: 代码、最新价、涨跌幅和市盈率列分别为 86、87、80、59px，均比对应的完整内容所需宽度少约 1px；行业列仅 39px，成交额列 72px 使表头换行不理想。

critique.good: 行业名称大多能按两个汉字一组阅读，名称与行业之间的视觉区分清楚。
critique.problems: 与 B 一样，代码和部分行情数值被拆开；名称逐字竖排，使多数行很高，也削弱了按股票名称查找的效率。成交额表头的括号被拆散。
critique.cause: 名称列仅 39px；代码、最新价、涨跌幅和市盈率列分别为 86、87、80、59px，略窄于完整内容所需宽度；成交额列为 72px。

critique.good: 代码、价格和涨跌幅完整；名称和大多数行业名称以两字一行显示，行高较均匀，便于横向查阅。
critique.problems: 多项成交额数值断行，妨碍准确读取和比较；成交额表头及单位被拆成四行，表头过高。
critique.cause: 成交额列宽62px不足以容纳最宽数值和内边距，也不足以让表头自然分行。

critique.good: 代码和四列行情数值均完整，成交额及其单位的表头关联清楚，数值比较可靠。
critique.problems: 股票名称和行业名称逐字竖排，识别缓慢，行距被显著拉大；所属行业表头也占四行。
critique.cause: 名称列55px和行业列51px都不足以并排显示两个汉字，导致标签逐字换行。

critique.good: 表格正好适配视口；股票代码、价格和带符号的涨跌幅保持完整，名称大多能按两个汉字一行辨认，数值列便于横向比较。
critique.problems: 所属行业和市盈率表头被拆成单字，行业名称也呈单字竖排；“汽车整车”将最后一行拉到四行，增加纵向查找距离。成交额与单位虽分行，关联仍然清楚。
critique.cause: 行业列50px的可用文本宽度不足以容纳两个汉字；市盈率列60px不足以容纳完整三字表头。名称列56px刚好跨过两个汉字的换行阈值。

critique.good: 表格适配视口，代码和行情数值仍保持完整，成交额与单位的关系清楚。
critique.problems: 名称和行业均大量单字竖排，名称表头也被拆开；多数数据行因此高达四行，股票定位和跨列阅读都明显变慢，空白在数值列中分布得较零散。
critique.cause: 名称列从56px缩至55px后跌破两个汉字同排的阈值；行业列51px仍不足以容纳两个汉字。市盈率列60px也使表头换行。

critique.good: Fits the viewport. Stock codes and numerical values remain whole, and the name and industry columns mostly use two-character lines. All six data rows have the same height, supporting scanning and comparison.
critique.problems: The turnover header is four lines tall, with the closing parenthesis stranded on its own line. This makes the header disproportionately deep and leaves substantial empty space in the other header cells. Several names and industries also break across lines.
critique.cause: The 67 px turnover column cannot accommodate the header in two lines. The 56 px name and industry columns accommodate only about two Chinese characters per line.

critique.good: Fits the viewport, keeps codes and numerical values whole, and presents the turnover header in two clearer lines with its unit.
critique.problems: The industry header and values read one character per line. Longer industries make the last two rows much taller, disrupting the otherwise regular scan of the table and increasing its height substantially.
critique.cause: Increasing the turnover column to 73 px takes 6 px from the industry column, leaving it at 50 px, too narrow for two Chinese characters side by side.

d2r0A.idea: 名称与行业均衡分配空间，同时给市盈率列额外余量，形成较均匀的中文换行节奏。

d2r0B.idea: 侧重股票名称识别，让名称有更多连续阅读空间，行业列承担更多换行。

d2r0C.idea: 侧重行业分类阅读，为行业列提供更宽空间，名称列承担更多换行。

d3r0A.idea: 在名称与行业之间较均衡地分配剩余空间，让两类中文标签共同承担换行。

d3r0B.idea: 优先加宽股票名称以便定位个股，让行业标签承担更多纵向换行。
notes: raised a column to the minimum 40px

d3r0C.idea: 优先加宽行业标签以便查看行业归属，依靠完整代码定位股票并让名称更多换行。
notes: raised a column to the minimum 40px

d1r0A.idea: 优先给股票名称空间以支持查找，将较多的中文换行集中在行业列。

d1r0B.idea: 优先给行业归属空间以支持分类浏览，允许股票名称更频繁地换行。

d1r0C.idea: 增加成交额列的空间以改善指标标题和数值区域的阅读，名称与行业采用较紧凑的多行排布。

d3r1A.idea: 保留代码、价格、涨跌幅和市盈率所需宽度，将名称和行业都提高到预计可容纳两个汉字的宽度；从成交额列取出空间，测试其数值是否仍能完整显示，以及表头和单位能否清楚换行。列宽合计 495px。

d1r1A.idea: 将名称和行业都调整到可容纳两个汉字的宽度，测试能否同时改善股票定位、行业阅读及行高；从成交额列腾出8px，观察较窄表头是否会拆开（亿），以及由此产生的可读性代价。

d2r1A.idea: 以B为基础，将名称列收至两字所需的临界宽度，把节省的10px给行业列。测试实际字体和边框下名称能否继续两字一行，以及行业表头或内容是否因此改善；同时保留代码和数值的完整宽度。

d3r2A.idea: 保留代码及所有行情数值的完整宽度，将名称列增至56px，使股票名称能够两字一行；行业列缩至50px，接受行业逐字换行，以改善更关键的股票定位和整体行高。

d1r2A.idea: 从名称列让出9px给行业列，保留完整行情数值和成交额单位；检验名称列能否仍以两个汉字一行显示，以及行业列增加的空间是否有实际效果。

d1r2B.idea: 进一步把8px从成交额列转给行业列，尝试让名称和行业都以两个汉字一行显示；代价是成交额中较长的数值及表头单位可能断开，需比较其可读性。

d2r2A.idea: 将名称和行业都调整到可容纳两个汉字的宽度，以改善行业阅读并缩短四字行业所在的行；成交额列收窄至 64px，需在实际渲染中检查其表头及“（亿）”是否被不自然地拆开。各数值列仍保留所测最长数值所需宽度，总宽 496px。

d3r3A.idea: 从成交额列移出6px，给行业列达到两个汉字同排的宽度；保留名称列的两字宽度及代码、价格和涨跌幅列的完整性。成交额表头可能增加换行，需在渲染中确认成交额数值仍完整，并检查表头高度与行业行高的整体变化。

d1r3A.idea: 将名称列的部分空间移给行业列，保留完整的行情数值和成交额单位。测试行业列能否以两个汉字为一行，以及名称逐字换行带来的行高代价是否值得。

d2r3A.idea: 保证成交额数值和单位完整，行业列容纳两个汉字；名称列缩至单字换行。检验以名称阅读换取数值完整和行业连续性的取舍。

d2r3B.idea: 同样保证成交额数值和单位完整，但保留名称列的双字换行，将行业列缩至单字换行。用于比较股票识别优先与行业阅读优先两种取舍。

d1r4A.idea: 将所属行业加宽至56px，尝试让行业名称和表头按两个汉字换行，同时保留名称列的两字宽度。所需6px从成交额列取得；需在渲染中检查较窄表头是否仍能保持“（亿）”完整，以及成交额数值是否完整。

d2r4A.idea: 保留d2r2A中较易识别的两字一行股票名称，将行业列收窄9px并转给成交额列。成交额数值和“（亿）”应能完整显示，代价是行业名称更可能逐字换行；需通过渲染核实。

d2r5A.idea: 将名称列缩至51px，给行业列增加5px。保留成交额列的完整数值和单位，并尝试让行业名称每行容纳两个汉字；代价是股票名称逐字换行，需要检视识别效率和行高。

contrast.idea: Equal widths fit the viewport but leave too little text space for the longest stock code, price and percentage change. Those identifiers and figures would have to break or overflow, impairing lookup and comparison.

contrast.why: Stock codes, prices and percentages break across lines, making lookup and comparison difficult. Equal columns leave some numeric cells spacious while splitting essential identifiers.

ref_auto.why: Codes and numeric values stay whole, but company names and industries run almost character by character down very tall rows. The resulting empty space makes scanning across rows slow.

d2r4A.why: Codes and numeric values remain intact, and names generally occupy two lines. The narrow industry column stacks characters vertically and makes the last rows disproportionately tall.

d1r4A.why: Codes, prices and percentages stay whole, and two-character industry entries fit on one line. Consistent row heights support comparison, though company names wrap and the turnover header breaks awkwardly over four lines.

acceptance.unsure: The precise severity of Chinese word breaks is partly a matter of editorial judgment; all four layouts appear to fit without clipping.

contrast.why: The equal columns split stock codes, prices and percentage signs across lines, making lookup and comparison laborious. The rows are consistent in height, but that regularity comes at a substantial reading cost.

ref_auto.why: Codes and numeric values remain whole, but company names and industries run one character per line. The resulting tall rows make it difficult to scan related fields and leave large empty areas in the numeric columns.

d2r4A.why: Codes and numeric values are intact, and company names mostly wrap in pairs of characters. The industry column is too narrow: its header and entries such as 半导体 and 汽车整车 stack one character per line, extending the last rows.

d1r4A.why: Stock codes and numerical values stay whole, while names and industries generally wrap in readable pairs. Uniform data-row heights aid scanning. The four-line 成交额（亿） header, with its isolated closing parenthesis, remains awkward.

acceptance.unsure: The renders support the ranking clearly. The severity of Chinese name and industry breaks is somewhat subjective, and the narrow viewport limits how natural all headers and labels can be at once.

ref_auto.why: Codes and figures stay intact, but company names and industries run one character per line. The resulting tall rows make scanning and comparing stocks laborious.

contrast.why: The compact rows come at the cost of splitting every stock code and several prices and percentages. Those breaks seriously impair lookup and comparison; the turnover header also breaks awkwardly.

d2r4A.why: Codes and financial values remain whole, and names are more readable than in A. The industry column still runs one character per line, producing very tall final rows and making industry lookup slow.

d1r4A.why: Codes and financial values remain whole, industries mostly read in pairs of characters, and uniform body rows support comparison. Company names still wrap, and the turnover header breaks across four lines with an isolated closing parenthesis.

acceptance.unsure: The measured word-break counts do not fully describe how disruptive each Chinese line break feels; the turnover header in D remains a conspicuous compromise.

d1r4A.why: Stock codes, prices and percentage changes remain whole, making the main figures easy to compare. Company names wrap, and the turnover header breaks awkwardly over four lines with a closing parenthesis alone.

L06.why: Every stock code breaks across two lines, making identifiers harder to scan and transcribe. The turnover header also leaves its closing parenthesis alone.

L01.why: Most key figures stay whole, but 000858 breaks after five digits. The four-line turnover header and wrapped names remain awkward.

L05.why: Stock codes and prices stay intact, but every percentage sign drops to a separate line, interrupting comparison of price changes. The turnover header is also fragmented.

L03.why: Codes and numeric values remain whole, but company names run one character per line. This makes identification slow and creates very tall rows with large empty areas.

L04.why: The compact header and even rows are visually orderly, and codes stay whole. However, two prices split across lines and every percentage sign is separated from its value, damaging financial comparison.

L07.why: Names and industries often run one character per line, while several prices, percentages and other figures split. The tall, sparse rows make both lookup and comparison difficult.

L02.why: All six stock codes break across lines, undermining lookup even though prices and percentage changes remain whole. The extra name-column width does not prevent the names from wrapping.

landscape.unsure: B and H differ slightly in column proportions, but their visible breaks and practical weaknesses are essentially the same. All layouts appear to retain their characters within the viewport; the main differences are in wrapping and usability.

L05.why: Codes and prices remain whole, but every percentage is separated from its percent sign. The turnover header occupies four lines, including an isolated closing parenthesis, and names and some industries also wrap.

d1r4A.why: Codes, prices and percentages stay intact, supporting lookup and comparison. Names and some industries wrap, and the four-line turnover header has an isolated closing parenthesis and makes the header disproportionately tall.

L04.why: The compact, even rows and shorter headers are visually orderly, but prices such as 1,438.00 and 356.20 break across lines, as do all percentages before the percent sign. This impairs financial comparison.

L06.why: Every stock code is split, sometimes after a different number of digits, making row lookup harder. Prices and percentages stay whole, but the turnover header is four lines tall and names wrap.

L07.why: Names and industry labels often run one character per line, while prices, percentages, turnover figures and a valuation also break within numbers. Tall, uneven rows make scanning and comparison difficult.

L01.why: Most codes and all prices and percentages stay whole, but 000858 breaks before its final digit. The four-line turnover header and wrapped names and industries also slow reading.

L03.why: Codes and financial figures stay whole, but every company name is stacked one character per line. This produces very tall rows with extensive empty space and makes name lookup laborious.

L02.why: All six stock codes break across lines, undermining lookup even though prices and percentages remain whole. The added name-column width does not keep the longest names on one line, and the turnover header remains four lines tall.

landscape.unsure: D and H have the same consequential code breaks and very similar visible quality; their small score difference should not be treated as a reliable preference. The ratings assess the supplied renders at this viewport and fixed type size.

d1r4A.why: Codes and numeric values stay whole and rows are consistent. Company names wrap, and the turnover header breaks across four lines with a closing parenthesis stranded on its own.

L11.why: Every turnover value splits its final digit onto a second line, making comparison difficult. The four-line turnover header and wrapped names add further friction.

L14.why: Numeric values remain whole, but the industry column forces labels into single-character lines. Longer industries make the last rows much taller and harder to scan.

L13.why: Two price-to-earnings values break across lines, including 23.8 and 112.3. The industry column gains width, but its longer labels still wrap and the turnover header remains awkward.

L08.why: Most six-digit stock codes split before the last digit, weakening the primary lookup column. The extra name width does not prevent the company names from wrapping.

L12.why: The turnover header reads more naturally in two lines and the shorter header improves proportions. However, 23.8 and 112.3 split in the price-to-earnings column, hindering comparison.

L10.why: Most figures and all codes remain whole, but the largest latest price splits its final digit onto a second line. Names still wrap despite their wider column, and the turnover header occupies four lines.

L09.why: Company names run one character per line, making stock identification slow and producing very tall, uneven rows with extensive empty space. Numeric values remain whole.

landscape.unsure: A and F involve a tradeoff: F has a much clearer turnover header, but A preserves all numeric values on one line. I give more weight to comparing the figures in this stock table.

L13.why: Stock codes and prices remain whole, but two P/E values break across lines. The turnover heading occupies four lines with an isolated closing parenthesis, and the P/E heading stacks one character per line.

L10.why: The first price breaks before its final digit, disrupting a key comparison column. The turnover heading is four lines tall, while names and some industries also wrap.

d1r4A.why: Codes and numeric values stay whole, supporting lookup and comparison. Names and longer industries wrap, and the four-line turnover heading with its isolated closing parenthesis makes the header disproportionately tall.

L12.why: The turnover heading is more compact and coherent than in C, but two P/E values split across lines and its heading stacks one character per line. That compromises numerical comparison despite the shorter header.

L08.why: Most stock codes break before their final digit, making the row identifiers difficult to scan and copy. The turnover heading is also four lines tall.

L14.why: Codes and numbers stay whole, but the industry column forces labels into single-character lines. Longer industries produce uneven, tall rows and substantial empty space elsewhere.

L11.why: Every turnover value breaks across lines, separating the final digit and making comparison difficult. The narrow turnover heading also runs to four lines.

L09.why: The name column stacks company names one character per line, greatly increasing row heights and separating each name from the values being compared. Most of the resulting row area is empty.

landscape.unsure: The relative severity of broken numeric values versus vertically stacked Chinese labels is partly a judgment about readers' priorities. All layouts fit the viewport and appear to retain their content.
